title: OSHA Technical Manual — Section VII, Chapter 1: Back Disorders and Injuries
version_effective_date: current OSHA online manual as accessed 2026-08-31
jurisdiction_scope: US federal guidance; does not create a universal manual-lift limit
notes: Supports multi-factor ergonomic risk assessment; not a stagehand-specific procedure.

title: Materials Handling — Heavy Lifting
jurisdiction_scope: US federal guidance/context; eTool creates no new OSHA requirements
notes: The eTool uses approximately 50 lb as a risk/control point in its electrical-contractor context. Crew Blueprint must not convert that figure into a universal stagehand weight limit or guarantee of safety.

title: Manual Materials Handling — Team Handling
jurisdiction_scope: Canada guidance; transferable ergonomics concepts only
notes: Supports deliberate coordination/leadership for team handling; exact commands and methods are not universal live-event rules.

title: Manual Materials Handling — General Practice
version_effective_date: fact sheet confirmed current 2025-01-21; page accessed 2026-08-31
jurisdiction_scope: Canada guidance; transferable manual-handling concepts only
notes: Supports checking for handling aids, route condition, load stability and task-specific handling needs.

title: Manual handling — Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992: Guidance on Regulations (L23)
jurisdiction_scope: Great Britain guidance/regulatory context; transferable ergonomic concepts only for Crew Blueprint US-facing synthesis
notes: Explicitly states there is no single correct way to lift and that technique does not replace broader risk-reduction measures; UK legal framework is not imported as US law.

title: Step 1: Identify Risk Factors — Ergonomics
role_scope: workers exposed to ergonomic risk factors
notes: Supports force, posture, carrying and excessive cart-pushing force as ergonomic risk factors.

title: 29 CFR 1910.176 — Handling materials — general
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where applicable
notes: Supports clear aisles/passageways, stable storage and storage-area housekeeping; does not define entertainment-production workflow ownership.

title: 29 CFR 1910.37 — Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where applicable
notes: Exact source for unobstructed workplace exit-route requirements where applicable.

title: 29 CFR 1926.416 — General requirements
jurisdiction_scope: US federal construction standard where applicable; not universal general-industry coverage
role_scope: covered electrical workspaces, cords and cables
notes: Supports keeping working spaces/walkways clear of cords that create hazards and rejecting worn/frayed cords in covered construction contexts. Applicability must be preserved.

title: 29 CFR 1910.334 — Use of equipment
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry where Subpart S applies
model_product_scope: portable cord-and-plug equipment and flexible cord sets within scope
notes: Supports damage prevention and visual-defect handling for covered flexible cords; not a general audio/video/fiber handling standard.

title: 29 CFR 1910.306 — Specific purpose equipment and installations
jurisdiction_scope: US federal general industry for covered specific-purpose installations
model_product_scope: covered flexible cords/cables and temporary installations
notes: Contains public-traffic guarding/protection provisions for covered contexts. Do not generalize its amusement/tent scope to every event cable route.

title: Optical Fiber Cable Installation Guideline

model_product_scope: Belden optical fiber cable installation guidance
notes: Demonstrates that fiber families can have product-specific bend/tension constraints; not a universal rule for every production cable.
